description: Backup and WAL-archive health. pgBackRest has no native exporter, so pgbackrest_metrics.sh writes a .prom file every 5 minutes into the node_exporter textfile collector on each Backup Server (10.0.0.30 for HQ, 10.1.0.30 for DR).

panels.title: Backup Success
panels.description: A valid successful backup exists for every selected stanza.

panels.title: Stanza Status
panels.description: pgBackRest `info` reported status code 0 for the stanza.

panels.title: Metrics Check
panels.description: 1 means pgbackrest_metrics.sh could not reach pgBackRest at all — every other value on this dashboard is then stale.

panels.title: Last Backup Age
panels.description: Full backups run weekly on Sunday 02:00, so anything over 8 days means a backup was missed.

panels.title: WAL Archive Age
panels.description: Time since the newest WAL segment landed in the repository. Growing here means PITR coverage is broken and pg_wal will fill up.

panels.title: Backups Retained
panels.description: repo1-retention-full=4, so a healthy repository settles at 4.

panels.title: Stanzas Monitored
panels.description: Expected: one stanza per site (pg_cluster_hq, pg_cluster_dr).

panels.title: Backup Age
panels.description: Sawtooth is healthy: it should drop to near zero every Sunday at 02:00 when the weekly full backup completes. A straight rising line means the cron job stopped running.

panels.title: WAL Archive Age
panels.description: Should stay low and flat. A rising line means archive_command is failing on the primary.

panels.title: Backups Retained
panels.description: Steps up after each backup and down when retention expires old ones. Settling at repo1-retention-full=4 is expected.

panels.title: Last Backup Timestamp
panels.description: Each step up is a completed backup.

panels.title: Repository Filesystem Used %
panels.description: The repository lives under /var/lib/pgbackrest. When this fills up, both backups and WAL archiving stop — and a failing archive_command backs WAL up on the primary.

panels.title: Repository Free Space
panels.description: Trend this against your weekly full backup size to predict when you run out of room.

panels.title: Repository Disk Throughput
panels.description: Write spikes mark the weekly full backup; the steady low write rate is incoming WAL.

panels.title: Backup Server Network Traffic
panels.description: Inbound traffic is WAL segments and backup data arriving over SSH.

panels.title: Backup Server CPU Busy %
panels.description: pgBackRest compression is CPU-bound and will peak during the weekly full backup.

panels.title: node_exporter Up (Backup Servers)
panels.description: If this is down, the pgBackRest metrics are not being scraped at all and every panel above freezes at its last value.

panels.title: Textfile Collector Errors
panels.description: node_exporter could not parse pgbackrest.prom. Usually a partial write — check that pgbackrest_metrics.sh still writes to a temp file and renames it into place.

targets.expr: sum(node_textfile_scrape_error{instance=~"$backup_server"} and on (instance) max by (instance) (pgbackrest_stanza_status{site=~"$site"})) or vector(0)

title: pgBackRest Backups — HQ & DR
